points.text: Benchmark small and curated for perfect agreement; may hide preference diversity and inflate metrics
Reproducibility brittle since candidate pool depends on proprietary editors
Online RL shown on one editor with one algorithm
No hyperparameter ablations or out-of-distribution edit-type stress tests
Self-ensemble cost, latency and memory not reported; no equal-budget comparison
Claim that reward variance aids optimization not causally established
RL experiments only on OmniGen2; other editors untested
Limited novelty: Flow-GRPO editing, variance-over-accuracy idea, self-ensemble all prior
Training data not released; hinders reproduction
Labeling with current models' candidates caps supervision where all models struggle
Section 6.4.1 compares different base models; reward model effect confounded
RL only on OmniGen2
Self-ensembling increases inference cost; trade-off not discussed
No comparison with other open-source reward models such as HPSv3, ImageReward
Claims of surpassing GPT-5 overstated; no confidence intervals or significance tests
Asymmetric comparison: EditScore ensembled K=4, proprietary models single-pass
Single-pass EditScore only matches its GPT-4.1 teacher
Circular evaluation: reward and metric share GPT-4.1 rubric; reward hacking not excluded
No human evaluation or reward-hacking checks of RL policy
Judge used for ImgEdit-Bench not stated
Causal claim that reward fidelity unlocks RL under-supported
Missing baseline RL with teacher model as reward on same setup
UniPic2 comparison uses different base model and recipe; not controlled
Table 4 equal RM accuracy with different RL outcomes contradicts narrative
No seeds or error bars for RL results
Pairwise accuracy metric under-specified: ties, chance level, below-chance consistency
Pairs not independent; effective sample size small; per-category numbers noisy
Benchmark tasks curated from same benchmarks used to evaluate RL
Possible overlap of training instructions/images with evaluation; no decontamination
Benchmark candidate pool includes outputs of RL base model OmniGen2
Novelty modest: assembled from existing components
No other editing reward model evaluated on new benchmark
No comparison to pairwise or Bradley-Terry reward model
Data filtering barely described and not ablated
Training and RL hyperparameter details insufficient
Efficiency claimed but unmeasured; Avg@4 multiplies reward cost
No analysis linking RM accuracy to RL outcomes across model sizes
RL tested on one base model and one algorithm
Presentation inconsistencies and typos
